heme_involvement_pattern.primary_compartment: peripheral_blood + bone_marrow + spleen + liver + lymph_nodes + skin

biomarkers.name: inv(14)(q11q32) or t(14;14) — TCL1A rearrangement
biomarkers.clinical_use: Defining hallmark abnormality; TCL1A IHC can be used as a surrogate

biomarkers.name: ATM mutations/deletions
biomarkers.clinical_use: Common genetic lesion; ATM dysfunction is frequent in T-PLL

biomarkers.name: Immunophenotype (CD2+/CD3+/CD5+/CD7+; usually CD4+/CD8-, sometimes CD4/8 double+)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinguishes from other mature T-cell leukaemias

biomarkers.name: CD52
biomarkers.clinical_use: Target of alemtuzumab — standard first-line therapy

biomarkers.name: JAK-STAT pathway mutations (JAK1, JAK3, STAT5B)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Recurrent cooperating lesions; rationale for JAK/STAT pathway inhibitor trials

biomarkers.name: t(X;14)(q28;q11) or t(Y;14)(q12;q11) — MTCP1 rearrangement
biomarkers.clinical_use: Alternative hallmark driver in TCL1-family activation when TCL1A rearrangement is absent

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Small to medium-sized T-cells with irregular nuclei, visible nucleoli, and cytoplasmic 'blebs' or protrusions; marrow, blood, spleen, liver, lymph node, skin, and occasional effusion involvement

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: CD52 expression commonly enables alemtuzumab therapy — the standard first-line despite associated infection risk
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Widespread infiltration — marrow, blood, spleen, liver, lymph nodes, skin, and serous effusions

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Mature post-thymic T cells (most often CD4+, less often CD4+CD8+ double positive, and occasionally CD8+) with distinctive TCL1-family activation
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Mature T-cell differentiation with small to medium-sized cells with irregular nuclei, visible nucleoli, and cytoplasmic 'blebs' or protrusions; TCL1A+ (or MTCP1+) enables leukaemogenesis
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: TCL1A activation (via 14q32 involvement with TCR loci) or MTCP1 activation drives this distinctive mature T-cell malignancy; JAK-STAT pathway mutations (JAK1, JAK3, STAT5B) are recurrent cooperating lesions
